rule: A top-level binding has one ID, `mod.name`, from its own file and from every importer, per C1. That covers `const`/`let`/`var`/`export const`, a function declaration and a class. A call through it uses that ID everywhere, never the bare name in its own file. | **Function literal.** The initializer is a function literal: a named function (existing rule). | **Alias.** The initializer, after removing parentheses, `as`, `satisfies` and `!`, is an identifier or member path that names a function (`isArray = Array.isArray`, `render = baseRender as RootRenderFunction`). The call resolves to that function's ID, as Lua/Zig aliases do. | **C1 Symbol identity.** Every definition has exactly one ID. Every reference to it uses that ID: a call in the defining file, through an import, a re-export, an alias or a `require` binding. | A definition that edges reach is listed in `nodes`, including body-less member declarations of scanned types (interface/trait/protocol methods) and module-level bindings that hold a function. A high edge's callee is always in `nodes`.
notes: Function-literal evidence: `add` (arrow), `sub` (function expression), `mul` (function declaration) and class `Acc` keep `core.<name>` in their own file and in the importer (never the bare name); calls to them are high. Alias evidence: `times = mul` resolves to `core.mul` (high: the target is defined in the scan; the 'Medium, not high' sentence explains the function-type/factory tiers, where only a binding was matched, whereas an alias resolves to the target's own definition, as the Lua/Zig alias decision does); `minus = (sub)` resolves to `core.sub` after removing parentheses; `toJson = JSON.stringify` (member path) resolves to the global `JSON.stringify`, medium. On use.js line 5 the six calls are toJson, add, sub, mul, times(->mul), minus(->sub).
